tex_content.html:
For $T'<T$ and $\epsilon >0$, outside a compact ball the flow on $[0,T']$ is $\epsilon $-close in $C^{[1/\epsilon ]}$ to $(S^2,h(t))\times (\Ar ^+,ds^2)$.
Proof

\sketch Take pointed limits along the initial cylindrical end. Derivative bounds and splitting give a product flow; positivity identifies its compact factor with the shrinking round $S^2$.

□

Corollary
[Maximal time is at most one]
